newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany backs U.S. on NATO enlargement - source.
newsitem.headline: Germany backs U.S. on NATO enlargement - source.

text.p: Germany supports a U.S. proposal to invite three ex-communist countries to join a first wave of NATO enlargement, a government official said on Friday.

But he said Bonn assumes the U.S. decision to offer early membership only to Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic means there will soon be a second round of enlargement to include other countries eager to join the alliance.
"It can be assumed that this smaller enlargement is a signal there will be a second round of enlargement soon," said the official, speaking on condition of anonymity.
The United States caught its NATO allies off guard during a defence ministers' meeting in Brussels on Thursday with the announcement that it favoured only three new members initially.
Although Washington's position is expected to be decisive, some of its European allies have vowed to fight on, at the alliance's July 8-9 summit in Madrid, for Slovenia and Romania to be invited in.
France and the supporters of a broader expansion argue that the two countries need to be included in order to maintain a balance between NATO's northern and southern flanks.
